Bingkun Qi · Academic Affairs System

My teaching list spanned several class sheets

Our weekly spreadsheet worked well for a form tutor. Each pupil had a row, with all their subjects side by side. I taught maths to some classes, physics to others and Further Mathematics to only some pupils. Pupils also joined partway through the term. Every reporting week I moved between sheets to find the right pupil and subject.

I asked the school office who taught each pupil in each subject. The office had only part of that picture, so I checked the assignments with every teacher and recorded them in a shared database. Subject teachers now write from their own teaching lists. Form tutors read the same comments by pupil and class.

Week 4 · Fictional pupil record

A physics comment and a missing maths report

The spreadsheet allowed a subject to be left blank if a pupil did not take it. Here the tutor can see that the pupil takes maths and a report is still due. The physics teacher has already left a specific comment.

One pupil, seen by two teachers

  1. The physics teacher records an observation — The pupil completed two of three homework tasks. The teacher records an overall C and adds a reminder to check how the pupil finds the intercept on a graph next lesson.
  2. The form tutor opens the same week — The physics grade and comment are visible in the pupil’s record. Alongside them, maths is marked “未填” (report pending).
  3. The tutor can follow up with two people — The tutor can ask the pupil to show how they read the intercept on their physics graph. For maths, the next step is to ask the teacher for the missing report.

Inside the Academic Affairs System

At school I saw colleagues switch between sheets less often. I also built tools for timetable changes, exams, homework and teaching hours. I have held back wider school use because it would involve more pupil data.

01

Weekly subject reports

The database retains the 11 feedback fields teachers knew from the spreadsheets. Each teacher gets a list of the pupils and subjects they teach and can copy the previous week’s entry before updating an observation.

02

The form tutor’s overview

Form tutors still read across subjects for their own class. The system compares each pupil’s enrolments with the subjects that have an overall grade for the week, so the tutor can see which teachers to follow up with.

03

Timetable changes

A change used to start with a message passed on through the head of academic affairs and the school office. With several Excel timetables in circulation, pupils, teachers and staff often had to ask which time was current. Teachers can now submit a change for approval, and staff and pupils can consult their respective views of the updated timetable.

04

Class lists and teaching assignments

I verified assignments at the level of an individual pupil and subject. When a pupil joins a class or changes course, the office can check their class, enrolments and teachers. These determine whose reporting lists the pupil appears on.

05

Exam and homework records

Teachers can record a mark, an analysis and advice for an exam, or completion and comments for a homework task. Both kinds of record can be retrieved by pupil to follow up a learning concern.

06

Teaching hours and exports

The system totals hours from the current timetable and extra lessons and exports the detail. This gives the school a starting point for reviewing teaching workloads. Historical cover and timetable changes still need to be reconciled under the school’s own rules.

Towards a continuing record for each pupil

Once the database was in place, I began to think about the next conversation with a parent. Could a teacher bring a classroom observation, a later piece of homework and a recent exam together to explain where a pupil had struggled and what had improved? That is what I want a pupil record to make possible.

Teachers and school staff

Follow a question over time

The physics teacher’s note about graph intercepts gives the tutor something specific to revisit with the pupil. Homework and exam records can already be retrieved by pupil. I would like teachers and tutors to follow that evidence over time, and authorised school staff to see where a pupil needs support.

Families

Give a parent a specific example

A tutor could select a piece of work that shows progress and another that shows what still needs practice. My aim is for the tutor to review those records before sharing them and agree a next step with the family.

Future development

Evidence of learning and pastoral care

Understanding a pupil’s grasp of a particular concept would require a link to the learning platform and evidence from relevant questions and responses. The pastoral module is a draft. Before including those records, the school would need to agree who may write and read them.

All pupil records and grades shown come from local demonstrations using fictional data.
